question: Following passage of a calcium oxalate stone, a 55-year-old male visits his physician to learn about nephrolithiasis prevention. Which of the following changes affecting urine composition within the bladder are most likely to protect against crystal precipitation?

options.opa: Increased calcium, increased citrate, increased oxalate, increased free water clearance
options.opb: Decreased calcium, increased citrate, increased oxalate, increased free water clearance
options.opc: Decreased calcium, decreased citrate, increased oxalate, increased free water clearance
options.opd: Decreased calcium, increased citrate, decreased oxalate, increased free water clearance
options.ope: Decreased calcium, increased citrate, increased oxalate, decreased free water clearance

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Decreased calcium -> Increased citrate -> Increased free water clearance -> 80% CHAIN: Increased citrate -> Increased urine pH -> Reduced crystal formation -> 75% CHAIN: Increased free water clearance -> Diluted urine -> Reduced crystal concentration -> 80%
analysis: To prevent crystal precipitation and reduce the risk of nephrolithiasis, it is important to increase citrate levels in the urine. Citrate acts as a natural inhibitor of crystal formation. Additionally, increasing free water clearance helps in diluting the urine and preventing crystal aggregation. Decreasing calcium and oxalate levels can also be beneficial as they are components of calcium oxalate stones.
